entries.summary: Yahoo Finance data retrieved 2026-11-05 00:30 UTC (about 6:30pm Chicago, after the US close; may be delayed up to 15 minutes) shows a broad-market gain with semiconductors lagging. SPY rose 1.65% to 766.81 and QQQ 0.97% to 691.95, while SMH fell 2.75% to 504.27. NVDA dropped 3.17% to 200.13, AVGO 2.0% and TSM 2.24%; AMD was the exception at +1.01% (488.78). The VIX fell 20.26% to 16.61, a sharp drop in implied volatility. I could not find a trusted article explaining this specific session, so the cause of the chip-versus-market divergence is not confirmed.
entries.movers: The VIX (-20.26%) and NVDA (-3.17%) moved most. Semiconductors sold off as a group (SMH -2.75%, TSM -2.24%, AVGO -2.0%) even as SPY gained, with AMD the lone chip name in the green.

entries.summary: Yahoo Finance data retrieved 2026-11-05 15:31 UTC (about 9:31am Chicago, right at the open; may be delayed up to 15 minutes) shows a sharp risk-off move led by semiconductors. SMH is down 8.09% to 463.48, AMD down 13.67% to 421.95, TSM down 7.79%, AVGO down 6.72% and NVDA down 6.44% to 187.23. The broad market is weaker too: QQQ is down 4.49% to 660.87 and SPY down 2.40% to 748.43. The VIX jumped 33.96% to 22.25, reversing the prior close's drop to 16.61. Bloomberg attributes the chip selloff to a rotation after the midterm elections and fears that tighter data-center regulation would hurt chip demand; early-open prints can swing quickly.
entries.movers: AMD (-13.67%) and SMH (-8.09%) fell most, with the VIX (+33.96%) spiking above 22. The whole chip group is down 6% to 14% at the open, a second day of selling after Wednesday's chip weakness.
